en: Portside hull has been\ndamaged. Shields are\nreduced to 40 percent.
All three ships remain\nlocked onto us. Weapons\nhot.
Launching pod three.
Pod has made it out of\nenemy ships' attack\nradius.

All crew members aside
from you, Captain, have
successfully been
evacuated.
Understood. Preparing the\nwarp drive.
...Four...three...two...one...
Commencing warp-out.
Enemy ships at six o'clock\nhave engaged warp drive.

They are operating at full
power. It will not be long
before they catch up with
us.

Federation borders are
nowhere in sight and
evacuation by pod is not
immediately feasible.
Red giant at two o'clock.\nAltering ship's trajectory.

There is a 32.2 percent
chance that using the
star's gravitational
acceleration to speed up
the ship will result in
failure.
I cannot recommend\nperforming such a\ndangerous maneuver.
...You are absolutely\ncertain?
Yes.
It's my only option.
Understood. Ship's\ntrajectory re-altered to\nenter red giant's orbit.
WARNING! WARNING!\nNavigation systems\ninoperable!
A force other than gravity\nis being exerted on the\nship.
It has disabled the warp\ndrive engines.
Sensors unresponsive...\nSubspace... distorted...\nTransporting ship...
Systems are back online.\nCommencing scan of ship.

Good morning, sleepyhead!
Although your vital signs
were stable, I was
beginning to worry that
nothing would wake you!
Wh-what is wrong!? Why\ndo you look so terrified!?

Oh, no! Could it be that
you are injured!? Tell me
where it hurts, Captain! Is
it a flesh wound!? Could it
be internal bleeding!?
Ugh! Get away from me!
Your googly eyes startled\nme.
Everything about you\ncreeps me out.
Wh-while I understand you\nare still a tad woozy, there\nis no need to be so rude...
Let us start over, shall\nwe? I am <font color=yellow>Coro</font>, also known\nas this ship's AI.

As such, it would be no
exaggeration to say our
fates are permanently
intertwi― ...Please do not
give me that look!

I am sure I will grow on
you! In time, you might
even start to think me
adorable!
Ignored, once again. *Sigh*\n...So you want to know\nwhere we are?
Let me see...

We appear to have
crash-landed on a planet
of some sort. I am,
however, unable to
identify the sector or
solar system we are in.

When the pirate ships
from earlier opened a full
assault on us, crew
members were evacuated
by pod; you attempted an
escape by warp drive.
This is where my records\nend.
I am currently attempting\nto ascertain the cause of\nour arrival here.
...What exactly happened\nto us?
...Will we ever be able to\nreturn to Earth?

You are right. Positively
correct. There is no time
to fret over such things.
We must find a way to
straighten this mess out.

I will begin scanning the
ship to determine how
much damage it has
sustained.

...I am unable to produce
any estimates. The
external sensors are
unresponsive.

Y-you are not thinking to
go outside, are you!?
Doing so would be
extremely dangerous!
You make a very\nconvincing argument.

Perhaps the only way for
us to determine the
extent of the damage is
by observing the ship
from the outside.

While this world, for the
most part, appears to be
habitable, please do be
careful.
Excellent. I can now see\nperfectly out of the\nmonitor in your collar.
The coast appears to be\nclear.
Wait.
There is something\nshining to your eleven\no'clock.
What is it? What is it?
Is everything all right?
The sensors are unable\nto identify the object.\nMaybe it is an explosive!
...Or, upon closer\ninspection, a mineral of\nsome kind?
It might have even been\nartificially manufactured.
If you bring it back to the\nship, I can run a full\nanalysis.
...Wait. Did you hear\nthat?
Ten o'clock! A humanoid\nlife-form is fast\napproaching!
Apparently it is being\nfollowed―no, chased―by\nsome massive creature!

Captain, no! Do not get
involved! To do so would
be a violation of the
<font color=yellow>Underdeveloped Planet
Preservation Pact</font>.
Captain! Captain!

Oh, no... Judging by their
trajectory, they will collide
with the ship. Perhaps you
will have no choice but to
intervene, after all...
You! Don't just stand\nthere gawping! Run!
...Is that what I think it is?
Raaah!

Heavens above--lend me
your powers that I might
forge a path for the
righteous!
...Another human!? What\nin the world is going on\nout there!?
*Pant*...*Pant*...
That spell has drained\nmuch of my strength from\nme.

The rest is up to you. I will
leave my summon in your
hands. Lead him in battle
and together fell the
enemy!
Make haste! I cannot keep\nhim here for much longer!

What does she mean by
'the rest is up to you'!?
And why is that boy not
going to be here for much
longer!?
Oh, dear! "Oh, dear! Miss!\nMiss!"
Are you hurt!?

Aargh! I do not know how
to begin processing this
situation...and multi-
tasking is supposed to be
my forte!
Captain, help!

Understood. Let us
engage in battle.
Eliminating the threat is
currently our top priority.

The young missus said
the boy she summoned
will listen to your
directives.
With him by your side,\nyou should be able to\ndefeat the enemy.

Excellent work. I must
admit you are quite a bit
more skilled than I had
anticipated.
Please sit back down,\nmiss! You appear to be\nunsteady on your feet...
I-I'm perfectly fine, thank\nyou!

This here is your ship,
correct? Would you
mind―er―taking me with
you?
M-miss! Are you all right?\nYou are teetering back\nand forth! You need help!
We are now in orbit\naround the planet.

Currently our shields,
communication system,
and a portion of our
sensors are down.

The engines and systems
regulating flight, however,
are online and functioning
normally.
I am using the positioning\nof the stars to navigate\nour ship.
The young lady we picked\nup is now asleep. Her\nvitals are steady.

I have run a scan of her
DNA and passed it
through the federation's
database.
...I was, however, unable to\nfind any matches.
It appears she is an\nunknown life-form.
Are you sure it is a good\nidea to keep her onboard?
It is the humane thing to\ndo.
I need to learn more about\nthat spell she used.
I couldn't leave a lovely\nyoung girl to fend for\nherself.

Indeed, you truly are
worthy of the title of
Captain! It is no wonder
you were so
well-respected among your
crew!
Ah, yes... The symbology\nshe used is unknown even\nto the federation.
It would indeed behoove\nus to learn more about it.
Love at first sight, eh?
It seems Cupid's arrow got\nour Captain right in the―

Aaah! No! Please do not
hit me! You cannot reset
me like you would a
broken TV!
The calculations are in. It\nwould seem we are\nlocated...

Se-seventy thousand
light-years from Earth!?
That is far outside the
federation's jurisdiction!
I-it cannot be! There must\nhave been a mistake!

Oh, dear! Oh, dear! Such a
grievous error is
unforgivable. I will be
chastised by my AI
brothers and then
decommissioned...

They will dump me in an
abandoned corner and
place a tarp over me.
There, I will slowly decay,
with only my fading
memories to keep me
company...
I am terribly sorry. I was in\nsuch a hurry that I must\nhave missed something.
I-I shall recalculate\neverything straight away!

I do not understand... No
matter how many times I
run the numbers, the
results remain the same.
...Perhaps it is as you\nsay―this is no mistake.

That means we are so far
out in space that I cannot
even determine which
sector we are in.

Perhaps we were sucked
into a wormhole? If that is
the case, our chances of
ever making it back to
Earth are...
Oh, but the odds do\nmatter, and very much so,\nat that!
You fail to understand\nthat nothing short of a\nmiracle will get us home!
...I apologize.

Your life span is far
shorter than mine. You
have much more to fear
than I, yet you are the one
consoling me... I am
ashamed.
I retract what I said\nearlier! Captain, we will\nfind a way back!
I shall attempt to\nconfigure a route to Earth.\nPlease stand by.

Configuration complete.
Please keep in mind,
however, that because we
do not have much data on
our current whereabouts,
this route is subject to
change.
I also will not be able to\npredict what we will\nencounter along the way.

This means we need to
travel the traditional
way―one star system at a
time.
We shall start by\njourneying to the adjacent\none!

Worry not, Captain. I will
be with you every step of
the way. Now let us make
for Earth.

You have discovered a
New Route. You can now
choose this New Route
from the Select Planet
screen.
